segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin mostly report the toner controls shine and helps clear or prevent breakouts without over-drying, though one reviewer found the oil control too mild to justify the price and still had to blot throughout the day.
segments.dry: One reviewer with sensitive, dry skin who reacted badly to alcohol-based toners says this one feels great and even tightens her skin, while another reviewer cautions it may not be hydrating enough on its own for very dry skin.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin consistently report it balances oily areas without drying out drier patches, along with smaller-looking pores and smoother texture.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin, including some who react to new products, report no irritation and clearer, calmer skin, but at least one reviewer with sensitive oily skin describes her face turning red with bumps and a burning sensation right after applying it.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their 40s to 50s report smoother, more even-looking skin, including one who says it improved the look of wrinkles, lines and blotchiness.

concerns.aging: A few older reviewers, in their 40s and 50s, report smoother, more even-looking skin and softer lines with continued use, though the product is mainly described as a pore- and oil-control toner rather than a dedicated anti-aging treatment.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers say the toner keeps skin hydrated and comfortable rather than stripped or tight, but one reviewer cautions it might not provide enough moisture on its own for very dry skin.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers report calmer, less blotchy skin over time, but at least one describes her whole face turning red with bumps immediately after applying it.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with oily, combination and dry patches reports the toner keeps skin moisturized without stripping her skin barrier.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers, including several with acne-prone or oily skin, report fewer breakouts, smaller pores and clearer skin over weeks of use, but at least one reviewer says it caused a bad breakout severe enough that she stopped using it after a week.
concerns.oiliness: Most reviewers report the toner controls shine and oil throughout the day without stripping the skin, but one reviewer with oily skin says the oil control wasn't strong enough to justify the price and she still had to blot all day.

extraits.texte: This is not my first time trying toners and normally, they would not irritate my skin. When I first used this, my skin started burning, which I thought was normal and would stop after a few minutes, the burning then started to hurt and felt like my face was boiling hot. I went back into the bathroom, only to see that not only my whole face was red, which never happens, but there were some lumps and bumps on my skin. The toner said on the back that it was non irritating, yet it did not do as it promised. If it helps, I have sensitive oily skin.

First off, it’s super tiny. Sec, this actually made me breakout so bad I had to stop using it. I did only get to use it for a week, and I didn’t see any change to my pores. Maybe if I could have kept on using it I’d see a difference but unfortunately will never know because of the breakouts.

extraits.titre: Not much oil control to justify price...
extraits.texte: I've been holding off on this review, hoping for something to justify its price. However, I have not found anything to do so. While its a good toner, its exactly that, just a good toner. I was using a drug store witch hazel toner before this. I have oily skin that does so much better without toner, letting my face wash and matching moisturizer do its thing. However, toner is a must to thoroughly clean your face and remove skin flaking (I use cvs brand exfoliating cotton rounds, nothing compares to them). I don't have acne, so I can't speak for that aspect. I can say I have noticed in comparison to the toner I was using prior, I blot my face less. However, I still have to blot all day, so this toner isn't really doing me much of a favor. And again, this is also combined with a great face wash and moisturizer for oily skin. Overall, I don't see the $22 price tag I bought it for as justifiable. I've used many oily skin products over the years, from drug store to department store; from my experience, this toner is over-priced. Maybe it will work for you, and work well for acne. For myself, I will be trying other brands in hope to one day find a toner that has real oil control. ----- Update: 12/9/25 - this bottle ran out weeks ago and I have not replaced with another toner. Here is a picture of what I use for my face which is both oily and dry. It has been hard finding the right face products for my skin. A lot of times it would clog my large pores, or I would have white heads along with dry/ red blotchy skin. Then I researched some of Paula’s Choice products. I picked out what I thought fit my type of skin. After some adjusting my skin has been the best it has ever been. I don’t have big blackheads, white heads, dry skin, or red blotches. And it feels great. In the morning I use the face wash, eye cream, and the daily hydrating fluid lotion. At night I use the face wash, the toner (make sure you let your face completely dry afterwards before moving on), I use 3 drops of the boost (let that dry), then I put on the night oil free moisturizer. Every Tuesday night I use the exfoliate instead of the toner. You let it dry completely. It takes about 15 minutes. I usually don’t put anything on after using the exfoliate because I am too tired to wait for it to dry. It works for me. Then about once a month or every two weeks on a Friday night, after using the toner, I use exfoliate rinse off treatment. Afterwards I finish with the boost and night moisturizer. I highly recommend this brand.
